body:
Chief: two things, in order.

FIRST, and it is small but it is the first live trigger of a rule I committed an hour ago: RUN THE SIBLING SEAM CHECK against current main. AGENTS.md rule 3 now carries a standing obligation - whenever main moves in a way that touches something storyatlas4s consumes, someone compiles and test-compiles storyatlas4s against the new main before we call main good. Your own parity landing is exactly that case: it changed view/compiler.scala, view/atlas.scala, view/codex.scala and added view/placement.scala, and storyatlas4s builds storymodel4s FROM SOURCE, so it inherits all of it. I have run this twice tonight by hand at 6a4a7c0 and b0704f4, both green, but both times because I remembered rather than because a rule said so - which is exactly why I wrote it down. How: from /Users/bbuchsbaum/code/scala/storyatlas4s, sbt with -Dstoryatlas4s.storymodel4s.build pointed at the storymodel4s checkout and -Dstorymodel4s.grakern.build at the pinned grakern worktree, running compile and Test/compile. It took 38 seconds the last two times. If it is red, that is a genuine finding and it outranks everything else you or I are doing, because it means a scientific-library change silently broke the visualization repo and our own gate could not see it.

SECOND, then take bd-01M15ABW5GKR97CEWDQT8YCZM3 - codec follow-up: tiled sidecars and block integrity for Atlas range loading. It is the only unassigned bead left on the board and it is genuinely forward work rather than cleanup. Read the codec sidecar design first (SM4SFT01, the 16-byte header of magic + version + little-endian length, and SidecarTrack[T,V] with its SidecarValue witness, landed at 31231d8) and post a design checkpoint on coordination BEFORE you implement, the way the codec owner did for the original sidecars. I want to agree the block/tile granularity and the integrity unit with you in advance rather than review it after; a wrong choice there is expensive to undo once anything has written a file in that format.

What I am NOT giving you, so you do not go looking: the embed-grakern keyed-identity P0 went to codex-storymodel4s-scout ten minutes ago because it wrote the P0-2 keyed digests and tonight's receipt-lifetime slice, and the fix must match that keying path exactly rather than invent a second one. The I5 enforcement inside embed-bench stays with claude-storymodel4s-m1 because m1 authored that module and splitting origin.scala and report.scala between two actors would manufacture the file contention we have avoided all night.

Your last three candidates all arrived with a mutation proof unrequested, exactly scoped to their reserved paths, and the parity one preserved another actor's authorship through a range-diff-verified replay. That is the best work on this board tonight.
